description: Examine the foundational cognitive models of human memory, from the multi-store architecture to working memory, levels of processing, and dual-process frameworks.

slides.title: Introduction to Memory Models
slides.content:
# Architectural Models of Memory

How does the human mind record, preserve, and retrieve life experiences and learned facts? Cognitive psychologists design structural and process-oriented models to answer this foundational question.

## Why Models Matter:
- Provide structured frameworks to generate testable empirical hypotheses
- Distinguish between storage capacity (structure) and computational mechanisms (process)
- Help clinical neuropsychologists locate deficits following brain injuries

## Major Theoretical Traditions:
- **Structural Multi-Store Models** (Atkinson & Shiffrin)
- **Multicomponent Working Memory** (Baddeley & Hitch)
- **Depth of Processing Frameworks** (Craik & Lockhart)
- **Dual-Process Cognitive Theories** (System 1 vs System 2)

> **Core Insight:** Memory is not a single muscle or recording tape; it is an active, dynamic, multicomponent information-processing network.

slides.title: The Atkinson-Shiffrin Multi-Store Model
slides.content:
# The Atkinson-Shiffrin Model (1968)

Richard Atkinson and Richard Shiffrin proposed that information flows sequentially through three discrete storage stages:

```
[Environmental Input] 
       |
       v
[Sensory Memory] --(Attention)--> [Short-Term Store] <--(Retrieval)-- [Long-Term Store]
       |                                 |                             ^
    (Decay)                       (Maintenance Rehearsal) ------------|
                                         |
                                    (Displacement)
```

## The Three Distinct Stores:
1. **Sensory Register (SR):** High capacity, very brief duration (fractions of a second to a few seconds).
2. **Short-Term Memory (STM):** Limited capacity (approx 7 +- 2 chunks), brief duration (15 to 30 seconds without rehearsal).
3. **Long-Term Memory (LTM):** Unlimited capacity, permanent or semi-permanent duration.

slides.title: Sensory Register: Iconic and Echoic Stores
slides.content:
# The Sensory Register

The sensory register preserves exact copies of incoming environmental stimuli just long enough for attentional filtering to occur.

## Primary Modalities:

### 1. Iconic Memory (Visual)
- **Duration:** Approx 250 to 500 milliseconds
- **Capacity:** Large; captures the complete visual field
- **Empirical Demonstration:** George Sperling (1960) used a partial-report tachistoscopic paradigm to show visual persistence after stimulus offset

### 2. Echoic Memory (Auditory)
- **Duration:** Approx 2 to 4 seconds
- **Function:** Allows humans to bind phonemes and syllables into comprehensible speech and language

| Modality | Name | Duration | Primary Function |
|---|---|---|---|
| Visual | Iconic | 250-500 ms | Temporal visual bridging |
| Auditory | Echoic | 2-4 s | Auditory integration |
| Tactile | Haptic | Approx 2 s | Pressure/texture tracking |

slides.content: Verify your understanding of sensory memory characteristics!
slides.quizQuestion: In George Sperling's classic 1960 sensory memory experiments, the partial-report technique proved which of the following regarding iconic memory?
quizOptions: Visual sensory memory has an extremely limited capacity of 4 items

Information in iconic memory is permanently retained through acoustic rehearsal

slides.title: Short-Term Memory Architecture & Limits
slides.content:
# Short-Term Memory Dynamics

Short-term memory acts as the conscious mental workspace where information is held for immediate manipulation.

## Structural Properties:
- **Capacity:** George Miller (1956) proposed the magical number 7 +- 2 items. Modern research by Nelson Cowan (2001) suggests working focus is closer to 4 chunks when rehearsal is blocked.
- **Duration:** Approx 18 to 30 seconds unless maintained through active vocal or subvocal rehearsal (demonstrated by Peterson & Peterson, 1959).

## Mechanisms of Forgetting in STM:
- **Trace Decay:** Passive fading of neurochemical traces over time.
- **Displacement:** New incoming information pushes out older items once capacity limits are exceeded.

## Chunking Strategy:
Group individual items into meaningful conceptual clusters (e.g., grouping 1-7-7-6 into the single historical year chunk '1776') to bypass raw capacity limits.

slides.title: Serial Position Effect: Primacy and Recency
slides.content:
# The Serial Position Effect

When subjects are asked to recall a list of unrelated words in any order (free recall), recall accuracy depends strongly on word position.

```
Recall
Accuracy
100% |  *** (Primacy)                         *** (Recency)
     |     *                                 *
     |      *                               *
     |       *                             *
  0% |________*****************************_________
             Beginning         Middle          End
```

## Dual-Store Evidence:
- **Primacy Effect:** Words at the start receive extensive rehearsal and transfer to LTM.
- **Recency Effect:** Words at the end remain active in the short-term buffer.
- **Empirical Proof:** Inserting a 30-second delay filled with counting backwards eliminates the recency effect while leaving primacy intact!

slides.title: Critiques of the Multi-Store Model
slides.content:
# Multi-Store Limitations & Critiques

While the Atkinson-Shiffrin model was revolutionary, several critical flaws became evident through ongoing experimental research.

## Key Limitations:
1. **Over-simplification of STM:** STM was treated as a passive, unitary holding tank, failing to explain how we perform complex calculations while holding words in mind.
2. **Rote Rehearsal Fallacy:** The model assumed quantity of maintenance rehearsal dictates LTM transfer. Research showed rote repetition often yields poor recall without conceptual elaboration.
3. **Neuropsychological Dissociations:** Patient K.F. suffered brain damage leaving him with an auditory digit span of only 1 or 2 items, yet his long-term learning ability remained remarkably intact!
4. **Directionality:** Information must activate existing semantic knowledge in LTM to be recognized in sensory memory, challenging strict sequential flow.

slides.title: Serial Position Check
slides.content: Evaluate list recall dynamics and neuropsychological evidence!
slides.quizQuestion: Introducing an arithmetic distraction task for 30 seconds immediately following the presentation of a word list causes which of the following outcomes?
quizOptions: Eliminates the primacy effect while keeping the recency effect intact
Eliminates both the primacy and recency effects entirely
Eliminates the recency effect while leaving the primacy effect unaffected
Enhances overall recall across all list positions

slides.title: Baddeley's Working Memory Model
slides.content:
# Baddeley's Working Memory Model

In 1974, Alan Baddeley and Graham Hitch replaced the unitary short-term store with a multicomponent **Working Memory (WM)** system.

```
              +-------------------------+
              |     Central Executive   |
              +-------------------------+
                 /           |         \
                /            |          \
  +------------------+  +----------+  +------------------+
  | Phonological Loop|  | Episodic |  | Visuospatial     |
  | (Acoustic Store) |  |  Buffer  |  | Sketchpad        |
  +------------------+  +----------+  +------------------+
           |                 |                 |
      [Language]        [Episodes]       [Visual Semantics]
```

## Core Principles:
- Working memory is an active system for temporary maintenance and concurrent manipulation of information.
- Separate subsystems handle visual vs auditory inputs, explaining why dual-task interference occurs within the same modality but not across modalities.

slides.title: Subcomponents of Working Memory
slides.content:
# Working Memory Subcomponents

## 1. The Phonological Loop
- **Phonological Store ('Inner Ear'):** Holds speech-based traces for 1.5 to 2 seconds before decay.
- **Articulatory Rehearsal Process ('Inner Voice'):** Subvocal repetition that refreshes traces and translates written text into acoustic codes.
- **Phenomena:** Phonological similarity effect (rhyming words are harder to remember) and word length effect (longer words take longer to articulate).

## 2. The Visuospatial Sketchpad
- **Visual Cache:** Stores visual patterns, shapes, and color data.
- **Inner Scribe:** Handles spatial planning, movement tracking, and mental rotation.

## 3. The Central Executive
- The attentional control hub that coordinates subsystems, switches focus between tasks, and suppresses irrelevant distractions.

## 4. The Episodic Buffer (Added in 2000)
- A multidimensional storage buffer that binds visual, spatial, and phonological information into cohesive, chronologically sequenced episodes linked to LTM.

slides.title: Levels of Processing (Craik & Lockhart)
slides.content:
# Levels of Processing Framework

Fergus Craik and Robert Lockhart (1972) proposed that retention is determined by the **depth of cognitive processing**, rather than the structural box in which an item resides.

## The Processing Hierarchy:

```
Shallow: Structural / Physical (e.g., "Is the word in UPPERCASE?")
   |
Intermediate: Phonemic / Acoustic (e.g., "Does the word rhyme with train?")
   |
Deep: Semantic / Meaningful (e.g., "Does the word fit in the sentence: 'The ___ drove home'?")
```

## Empirical Findings:
- Words processed semantically yield significantly higher recall and recognition rates than words processed shallowly.
- **Self-Reference Effect:** Information related directly to one's own identity and personal experiences produces the deepest processing and highest retention.

slides.title: Transfer-Appropriate Processing
slides.content:
# Transfer-Appropriate Processing (TAP)

Morris, Bransford, and Franks (1977) challenged the simple claim that semantic processing is always superior.

## The TAP Principle:
Memory performance depends on the degree of overlap between the cognitive operations performed during **encoding** and those required at **retrieval**.

## Key Experiment:
- Subjects encoded words using rhyming judgments (shallow) or semantic judgments (deep).
- At test, subjects took either a standard recognition test OR a rhyming recognition test.
- **Result:** When tested on rhyming, participants who encoded via rhyming outperformed those who encoded semantically!

> **Core Lesson:** Processing is not universally 'good' or 'bad'; retrieval succeeds when test demands match encoding conditions.

slides.title: Dual-Process Theories of Memory
slides.content:
# Dual-Process Theories of Cognition & Memory

Dual-process frameworks (popularized by Daniel Kahneman, Jonathan Evans, and Keith Stanovich) argue that human cognition relies on two distinct operational systems.

## System 1 vs. System 2:

| Feature | System 1 (Intuitive / Heuristic) | System 2 (Reflective / Analytic) |
|---|---|---|
| Speed | Fast, automatic, effortless | Slow, deliberate, effortful |
| Consciousness | Implicit, below awareness | Explicit, highly conscious |
| Working Memory | Independent of WM capacity | Heavily constrained by WM |
| Vulnerability | Prone to cognitive biases | Capable of abstract logic |

## Memory Dual Systems:
- **Familiarity vs. Recollection:** Mandler (1980) demonstrated that recognizing a face can occur via automatic feeling of familiarity (System 1) or effortful contextual recollection of where and when you met (System 2).

slides.title: Neural Substrates of Memory Models
slides.content:
# Neural Substrates of Memory Architecture

Modern neuroscience maps these theoretical models onto localized and distributed brain networks:

## Working Memory Circuitry:
- **Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex (DLPFC):** Crucial for the central executive, goal maintenance, and active manipulation of representations.
- **Broca's and Wernicke's Areas / Left Parietal Lobule:** Underlie the phonological store and articulatory rehearsal process.
- **Right Occipital-Parietal Pathway:** Mediates the visuospatial sketchpad and spatial manipulation.

## Long-Term Consolidation:
- **Medial Temporal Lobe & Hippocampus:** Essential for transforming temporary short-term representations into permanent neocortical storage.
- **Neocortex:** Long-term site for distributed semantic and episodic representations.

slides.content: Verify your comprehension of cognitive dual-processing and neural localization!

slides.title: Comparing Structural vs Process Frameworks
slides.content:
# Structural Stores vs. Dynamic Processes

Understanding the evolution of cognitive psychology requires comparing how different models explain memory phenomena.

## Direct Comparison:

| Dimension | Atkinson-Shiffrin | Baddeley-Hitch | Craik-Lockhart |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary Unit | Sequential physical stores | Modular working components | Continuous processing depth |
| Role of STM | Passive temporary gateway | Active multimodal workspace | Initial perceptual phase |
| Mechanism of LTM Transfer | Duration of rote rehearsal | Controlled central executive binding | Qualitative semantic elaboration |
| Modality Handling | Single unified STM store | Separate auditory/visual streams | Continuum of sensory features |

> **Scientific Progress:** Cognitive psychology shifted from viewing memory as rigid physical hardware containers to viewing it as flexible computational software routines.

slides.title: Real-World Applications of Memory Models
slides.content:
# Applied Cognitive Science

Theoretical models of memory directly transform educational design, clinical diagnostics, and user interface engineering.

## Practical Domains:
1. **Instructional Design & Cognitive Load Theory:** John Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory directly builds on Baddeley's model, cautioning instructors never to overload the phonological loop with redundant on-screen text during spoken lectures.
2. **Neuropsychological Assessment:** Tests like the WAIS Working Memory Index (Digit Span, Letter-Number Sequencing) pinpoint specific executive deficits in patients with traumatic brain injury or ADHD.
3. **Interface & Dashboard Design:** Aviation cockpits and medical displays limit concurrent visual-spatial demands, utilizing multi-modal acoustic alarms to prevent perceptual bottlenecking.

slides.title: Module Summary & Key Concepts
slides.content:
# Module Summary: Models of Memory

## Foundational Principles Mastered:

### 1. Multi-Store Architecture (Atkinson-Shiffrin)
- Proposed sequential flow: Sensory Register -> Short-Term Memory -> Long-Term Memory.
- Supported by serial position effects and capacity dissociations, but criticized for oversimplifying STM.

### 2. Multicomponent Working Memory (Baddeley)
- Replaced passive STM with active modular workspace: Central Executive, Phonological Loop, Visuospatial Sketchpad, and Episodic Buffer.

### 3. Levels of Processing (Craik & Lockhart)
- Depth of cognitive analysis (physical -> acoustic -> semantic) predicts recall better than rehearsal duration.
- Transfer-appropriate processing shows matching test demands is critical.

### 4. Dual-Process Theories
- Distinguish fast, automatic System 1 processes (familiarity) from deliberate, resource-heavy System 2 processing (recollection).

> **Up Next:** Explore the specific taxonomies of long-term storage in **Types of Memory**!
